title: Value Elasticity Surface (VES): dynamic prioritization for token-cost and latency-sensitive roadmap
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Problem: Existing RICE-like heuristics at Redwood surface static ordinal scores that miss workload-dependent tradeoffs between token cost and latency sensitivity. For runtime and console roadmap decisions we need a continuous prioritization surface that accounts for: variable traffic shapes, customer SLAs, per-route token economics, and OKR-aligned value multipliers.

Proposal: Build a Value Elasticity Surface (VES) — a prioritization framework and lightweight tooling that computes a two-dimensional surface for each initiative representing marginal value per unit of token-cost and marginal value per millisecond of latency change. VES combines: a) value signals (R/Reach x Impact proxies x confidence), b) workload elasticity models (how change in latency or cost changes conversion/retention), and c) operational constraints (capacity, rollout risk). The output is a ranked set of candidate roadmap items for the coming cycle with scenario-aware bucketing (conservative/expected/aggressive).

Why different: Rather than forcing a single composite score, VES exposes tradeoffs as contours so PMs can select items aligned to OKRs (e.g., revenue vs. reliability) and engineers can see expected infrastructure delta. It supports multi-scenario evaluation, ties back to token-level cost estimates from Redwood Optimize, and is built to plug into our OKR/initiative tracker and the Console roadmap view.

Deliverables:
- VES spec and calculation notebook (Google Sheets + Python prototype)
- Integration connector that consumes per-route cost/latency profiles and outputs ranked candidate lists
- Small Console UX mock to visualize top contours for initiatives
- Playbook for PMs to interpret VES scores and map to OKRs and releases

Success metrics:
- PM/Eng alignment time for roadmap decisions reduced by 30% (survey)
- 2 pilot initiatives re-ranked by VES in next cycle, with A/B check on cost or latency improvement attribution
- Console view adoption by 3 product teams in first quarter after launch
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published and reviewed by Eng, Research/Applied ML, and Design
Prototype notebook that computes VES for at least 4 representative initiatives using historical traffic samples
Connector that maps Console per-route token/latency metrics into VES inputs (cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95 latencies)
UX mock available and validated with two PMs and one design critique
Playbook with step-by-step decision flow and example mappings to OKRs published in Drive
